sentence: The NHS describes paracetamol as a painkiller that is also used for a high temperature.
note: Page title: 'painkiller for pain and high temperature'.

sentence: It is used to treat mild to moderate pain.
note: About page summary: used to treat mild to moderate pain.

sentence: The NHS lists headaches, joint swelling and stiffness, cold or flu symptoms such as fever, toothache and sore throat among the things it can ease.
note: Summary of main NHS page listed these uses; summary blended pages, attribution to main page reasonable.

sentence: Paracetamol is sold in pharmacies and shops.
note: About page summary: sold in pharmacies and shops.

sentence: For long-term pain, a larger tablet strength may be available on prescription.
note: About page summary: 1g tablets on prescription for long-term pain (number omitted).

sentence: It also comes as capsules and as a liquid, as the product leaflets for UK brands show.
note: emc results titled 'Paracetamol 500mg Capsules' and 'Paracetamol 500mg/5ml Oral Solution' SmPC; tablets named in leaflet titles.

sentence: Paracetamol is also one ingredient in some combined painkillers, such as co-codamol, which pairs it with codeine.
note: Result title: 'Co-codamol for adults: painkiller containing paracetamol and codeine - NHS'.

sentence: The NHS says other medicines containing paracetamol, such as some cold and flu remedies, should not be taken alongside it because of the risk of overdose.
note: About page: do not take with other products containing paracetamol, overdose risk; side-effects summary named cold and flu remedies.

sentence: The NHS says paracetamol seems to work by blocking chemical messengers in the brain that tell the body it is in pain.
note: Summary of NHS common-questions result: blocks chemical messengers in the brain that signal pain. Blended summary; wording 'seems to' kept.

sentence: It also lowers a high temperature.
note: Summary: also lowers a high temperature; main page title says pain and high temperature.

sentence: A dose can take up to an hour to start working, and the effect lasts for some hours.
note: Summaries: relief can take up to an hour; keeps working for about five hours (number omitted).

sentence: The NHS says paracetamol can be taken with or without food, and that people can eat and drink normally while taking it.
note: Summary: tablets can be taken with or without food; adults page says eat and drink normally.

sentence: Product leaflets say some medicines can change how paracetamol behaves in the body.
note: Summary of emc results: some drugs can change how paracetamol behaves in the body.

sentence: Product leaflets say medicines that speed up the stomach, such as metoclopramide and domperidone, make paracetamol be absorbed faster.
note: Summary of emc SmPC results: metoclopramide or domperidone speed absorption.

sentence: Too much paracetamol can damage the liver, according to the NHS.
note: Common-questions and NHS 111 Wales summaries: too much can damage the liver.

sentence: The NHS says paracetamol rarely causes side effects when it is taken correctly.
note: Side-effects page summary: rarely causes side effects when taken correctly.

sentence: The main serious ones are an allergic reaction, liver problems and a problem with blood cells.
note: Side-effects summary lists these three.

sentence: Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing or swallowing, can be signs of a serious allergic reaction, and the NHS says to call 999.
note: Summary: call 999 if lips, tongue or throat swell or struggle to breathe or swallow.

sentence: Feeling sick and yellowing of the skin or eyes can be signs of liver problems, and yellowing may be harder to notice on black or brown skin.
note: Summary: warning signs include feeling sick and yellowing of skin or eyes; harder to notice on black or brown skin.

sentence: Easy bruising or nosebleeds can be signs of a blood cell problem.
note: Summary: blood cell problems show as easy bruising or nosebleeds.

sentence: For these liver or blood signs that are not an emergency, the usual route is a GP appointment, or NHS 111 if they need attention the same day.
note: Site signposting rule; the returned text did not name the route for these signs.

sentence: Taking an extra dose is unlikely to cause problems, the NHS says, but it advises getting medical advice because too much can sometimes damage the liver.
note: Summary: extra dose unlikely to cause problems but important to get medical advice as it can sometimes damage the liver.

sentence: The NHS says paracetamol should not be taken with other medicines that contain paracetamol, because of the risk of overdose.
note: About page: do not take with other products containing paracetamol.

sentence: Medicine leaflets say that alcohol and some other medicines, such as barbiturates and tricyclic antidepressants, may raise the risk of liver harm, especially after an overdose.
note: Summary of emc results: enzyme-inducing drugs such as barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol may increase liver toxicity, especially after overdose.

sentence: The leaflets also say that taking paracetamol for several days may raise the risk of bleeding in people on anticoagulants.
note: Summary of emc results: anticoagulants, several days of paracetamol may increase bleeding risk.

sentence: NHS 111 Wales advises people who take warfarin to talk to a doctor, because regular paracetamol can raise bleeding risk.
note: Summary of NHS 111 Wales page.

sentence: On alcohol, the NHS says a small amount is usually acceptable with paracetamol.
note: Summary: drinking a small amount of alcohol while taking paracetamol is usually safe (word 'safe' not reproduced).

sentence: It adds that drinking may not be suitable for people with some conditions, such as liver problems, and points to the leaflet in the pack.
note: Summary: may not be safe with certain conditions such as liver problems; check leaflet.

sentence: Leaflets say regular heavy drinking raises the risk of harm at overdose levels.
note: Summary of emc results.

sentence: The NHS says most adults can take paracetamol, but it is not suitable for everyone.
note: Summary of main NHS page.

sentence: It lists people who have had an allergic reaction to it, people with kidney or liver conditions, and people who are dependent on alcohol or binge drink.
note: Summary of main NHS page.

sentence: NHS 111 Wales says people with a low body weight may need a lower dose and should check with a doctor or pharmacist.
note: Summary: under a weight threshold, check with doctor or pharmacist; threshold omitted.

sentence: The NHS says paracetamol can be taken during pregnancy and while breastfeeding at the recommended amount.
note: Summaries of About page and NHS 111 Wales.

sentence: Product labels add that it should be used at the lowest effective amount for the shortest possible time in pregnancy, and that studies on children's brain development after exposure in the womb have been inconclusive.
